**Gaps — no SOP yet**

• **Member Onboarding** – first 7 days experience (goal-setting, induction class, app setup, payment confirmation, welcome touchpoint). Currently ad-hoc; leaks early retention.
• **Cancellation & Churn** – trigger-based win-back (who contacts when, what offer, escalation path). No playbook means revenue walks silently.
• **Class Quality Audit Checklist** – coaching consistency measurement (music levels, cue quality, form correction, energy, time management). Without this, "coaching standards" exist only on paper.
• **Member Checkins** – cadence & script for 30/60/90 day check-ins (progress review, goal reset, upsell trigger). Retention depends on this.
• **Member data privacy & GDPR** – consent capture, data storage, deletion requests, breach protocol. Legal/reputational risk if absent.
• **Supplies & Sundries ordering** – reorder triggers (towels, water, supplements, cleaning stock), vendor management, budget owner. Studio downtime hits membership perception.
• **Referral Programme** – mechanics, who qualifies, how to promote it to members, reward fulfilment. Low-cost acquisition sitting unused.
• **Pause vs. Cancellation SOP** – eligibility, duration limits, re-engagement sequence post-pause. Conflated with cancellation now.
• **Complaint & Incident Escalation** – H&S incidents, member complaints, coach misconduct, payment disputes. No formal log or resolution path.
• **Milestone Achievements** – how you track and celebrate member wins (transformation photos, strength PRs, attendance streaks). Drives retention and word-of-mouth.

# THE FORGE — FRACTIONAL CFO ACTION PLAN

## REVENUE — CRITICAL PRIORITY

- **July collapse is an emergency:** Revenue crashed 92% month-on-month (£17,711 → £1,363). Active clients stayed at 151, so this is almost certainly a data error (incomplete month, system glitch, or holiday closure). Verify immediately — if real, you've lost £16,348 in a month. Assuming it's partial data, your *actual* trend Q2–Q3 (May–July vs Feb–Apr) shows: £54,158 → £39,272, down 27.6%. That's a serious decline despite the bigger studio and zero churn in June.

- **Pricing & upsells are your lever:** Average Revenue per Member (AR/M) has fallen from £170 (Dec peak, best case scenario) to £120 (June) — a 29% drop. You're not charging enough or members aren't buying add-ons. Implement tiered memberships (basic/premium/platinum) immediately; introduce 4-week personal training blocks at £80–120; add nutrition coaching or retail (protein, accessories). Target AR/M back to £160+ within 90 days.

- **Attrition spiked post-relocation:** Churn was 8.33% in April (relocation month, understandable) then 5.74% (May), 0% (June), then vanished data (July). But Feb–Mar averaged 4.74%, so current baseline is elevated. Run exit surveys; offer "welcome back" re-activation discounts to lapsed members (cheaper than new acquisition). Target churn below 3%.

- **Quiet class utilization:** With 151 active clients and a studio twice the size, you should be running more sessions or higher-density classes. If capacity is being wasted, consolidate quiet sessions or introduce off-peak pricing (7 am / 6 pm classes £2–3 cheaper) to smooth revenue across the day.

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**Before you build the menu:**
- Audit what you're *actually* delivering right now across all coaches. Document every variation, add-on, and "we sometimes include that." You'll find inconsistencies killing your margins and confusing members.

**Structure it in two layers:**
- **Member-facing**: Price tiers with outcome language, not features ("Transform in 12 weeks" beats "12 group classes + 1 PT session"). Include what's *excluded* — clarity on what's NOT in basic membership stops scope creep complaints.
- **Coach-facing**: The operational reality — exact what they deliver at each membership level, what requires upselling, which classes they run. This is your quality-control document.

**Price it strategically, not evenly:**
- Don't default to three tiers. Test: basic group classes only → mid-tier (groups + 2 PT sessions/month) → premium (unlimited PT). Price the mid-tier to be the "obvious choice" — it should capture 60% of sign-ups because it feels like better value than it actually is.

**Lock it down digitally immediately:**
- Get this into your booking system (Mindbody, Zen Planner, whatever) so coaches can't override it. Automate email confirmations showing exactly what they've bought. Stops "but I thought that was included" disputes dead.

**Launch with your coaches first:**
- Workshop the menu with them before members see it. They'll spot delivery issues and pricing gaps you'll miss. Their buy-in means they'll upsell it properly.

What's your current membership structure — is it just one flat rate or already tiered?

# The Forge — Fractional CFO Commentary & Action Plan

## REVENUE — GROWTH STALLING & CHURN SPIKE IS THE ALARM

**Your biggest problem right now:** May's 12.8% churn is catastrophic and erased all of April's member growth (+13 to 134). July bounced back to 142 members, but you're fighting a retention leak.

- **Pricing & upsells are undercooked.** Rev/member has flatlined at £120–139 across six months. With 142 active members, you should be hitting £20k+/month if you had a tiered offering (intro classes £59, unlimited £79, premium personal training add-ons, retail). Benchmark gyms 60% larger are doing £25k. **Action: Audit your pricing—introduce a PT add-on package (£40/month) and test a 5-class/month tier at £49 to capture price-sensitive new joiners. Target +£2k/month within 8 weeks.**

- **Churn baseline is 5.1–6.2% (Jan–Mar), then spiked to 12.8% in May.** Something broke in May (post-relocation onboarding, staffing change, class cancellations?). **Immediate action: Pull churn by reason from TeamUp—interview the 17 members who left. If it's class timetable or instructor, fix it now. If it's post-move friction, implement a 30-day new-member check-in call (staff-led, not email).**

- **July revenue £19,764 on 142 members is your best unit economics** (£139/member). Replicate that intensity: which classes fill, which staff ran them, was there a promo? Document and repeat.

---

## EXPENSES — RELOCATION HIDDEN THE REAL COST BASELINE

**Excluding April's relocation spend, average cash out is £17.9k/month (Feb, Mar, May–Jul). You're not breaking even every month.**

- **Cash burn in March (£-5.3k) and June (£-2.5k) suggests seasonal cost spikes.** Likely: rent uplift post-move (new lease higher?), rates revaluation, or utility jump in heating months. **Action: Line-by-line P&L for June—isolate rent, utilities, insurance, payroll. Target: rent should be ≤40% of revenue (currently £19.7k July revenue = rent cap £7.9k). If you're above that, renegotiate or challenge the move ROI.**
